human_reorganization: The paper reconstructs the smooth Tanaka approximation, original L2 identification, compact maximal estimate, summable path subsequence, supported Stieltjes mass, inverse-clock measure transport and observed martingale proofs. The Brownian predictable isometry and smooth Ito formula are stated foundational inputs, also present in the frozen library.

The paper normalizes the continuous mass to zero on a measurable exceptional event, whereas the source centers its Stieltjes cumulative there. These agree on a common probability-one event, so the same original coordinate classes and actual-process conclusions are retained. No new Lean declarations are added.

The printed bounded-sampling proof uses integrable compact maxima of the particular Brownian, sign-integral and compensated-square martingales. The formal generic sampling theorem instead uses uniform integrability and requires no such additional maximum hypothesis. The paper does not claim to prove that more general theorem.

Causal raw-past clock versions are distinguished from actual coordinates measurable in ambient null augmentation. No right-continuity, driver-independence, Markov all-start family, generator identification or stochastic flow is assumed.
Holding identity has one common path event for every parameter and horizon. Nontrivial holding is asserted in positive expectation/probability, not samplewise positivity or a computed terminal atom.

The two-source balanced pair is included in the same paper. Its complete finite-increment Fourier law is proved by bounded stopped phase products, rather than inferred from one-time marginals. Brownian-coordinate path laws do not silently assert a Brownian property in the joint pair filtration. Positive covariance is for every positive terminal time; diagonal mass is asserted at some deterministic time in every horizon.

The atomless temporal Stieltjes mass becomes L_T delta_0 under the Brownian observation, on one common event for all horizons. Positive probability of failure of spatial absolute continuity is an explicit classical human deduction from positive expectation; no every-sample positivity is asserted.

Two distinct Borel probability kernels disintegrate the same actual initial pair law delta_(0,0), agreeing only at the observed state zero. The constant kernel fails the all-start time-zero identity. This is a version warning, not semigroup or martingale-problem nonuniqueness.

Section 12 proves the complete Hermite conditional identity with dominated differentiation and bounded sampling. The observed-past Hermite theorem is already mapped in the source. Operational time cannot be replaced by physical time even for the second Hermite polynomial.

The boundary martingale source has augmented physical-past filtration. The printed observed-past extension is a human deduction from prefix Riemann-sum measurability and shrinking the filtration. The factor 2*kappa*g(0) is derived using the exact original Tanaka and half-Laplacian conventions, including kappa=0 without division.

The radius boundary test has linear growth and a derivative jump. Its martingale identity is not a C0 closed-generator domain identification or martingale-problem uniqueness theorem. The nonsticky Gaussian terminal-law pairing obstruction does not classify invariant measures.

Section 13 reconstructs the actual C0 sticky differential relation, boundary slope maximum principle, uniform resolvent uniqueness/stability and a genuine dense closable graph for kappa>0. Smooth compact tests constant near zero are uniformly dense but have generator value zero there. The explicit vanishing pair F=(1+kappa/4)sqrt(1+x^2)-(1+kappa/2)sqrt(4+x^2)+(kappa/4)|x| has G(0)=1/4 and the exact sticky slope jump, so every flat-test output remains at uniform distance at least 1/4. This excludes a graph-core identification, including in any closed extension containing that pair. Value density and closure give no resolvent range, all-start transition generator or uniqueness theorem. The fixed gap itself also holds at kappa=0, while the named closability estimate retains kappa>0.

Section 14 adds the actual whole-path Borel equivalence and complete operator-domain transport. A fixed smooth-mass subsequence produces a raw Borel continuous-path functional; a monotonicity replacement gives an everywhere defined clock and path map agreeing with the actual construction. Full observed-path recovery plus a countable raw-version/factorization argument gives a Borel inverse modulo the respective path laws. Both pushforward measures and almost-sure inverse directions are proved before composing L2 classes. The resulting real L2 map is onto, preserving norms and means. For supplied dense T into a fixed Hilbert codomain, the transported domain is exactly U^-1 D(T); density and closedness are equivalent, and D((TU)^*)=D(T^*) with value U^-1 T^*. Graph-core transport is explicitly a HUMAN graph-norm consequence. The printed raw factorization and Cauchy-set totalization reorganize the existing version lemmas without claiming new formal definitions. No equality of the laws in the same coordinates, physical-time filtrations, prescribed SDE drivers, physical generators, or all-start transition families is inferred.
